title: Building a Box That Cannot Decide If It Contains Itself
concept_layer: Russell's paradox; self-reference as contradiction; limits of naive set theory; infinite regress made tangible
technique_reference: XR ray pickable interaction (jelly_cube, rotation_gimbal controls)
domain_deferred: type theory as the fix → deferred (not in current spine)

capture_leaks.concrete_not_abstract: The box is a tangible demo. Russell's actual paradox is about ALL sets — infinitely many, not a chain of containers. The physical analogy leaks.
capture_leaks.finite_regress: max_visible_depth bounds the chain. Mathematical regress is unbounded. The ∞ indicator is a nod, not the thing.
capture_leaks.decidability_confusion: The box ‘cannot decide’ visually (paradox animations), but that’s different from Gödel-undecidability (there exist statements neither provable nor disprovable in the system).
capture_leaks.naive_set_theory_specific: This paradox broke Cantor’s naive theory but ZFC fixes it via the axiom of foundation. The artifact doesn’t explain the fix — that’s a separate artifact.
capture_leaks.metaphor_limit: Self-reference in language (‘this sentence is false’), code (recursion), sets (Russell), and arithmetic (Gödel) are different kinds of self-reference. The box handles only the set version.

limit: A box that opens to reveal another box, forever. What it captures: the visceral experience of infinite self-reference. What it refuses: the specific mathematical formulation that made Russell’s paradox a crisis (undefined sets, comprehension axiom), the historical context (Russell’s letter to Frege destroying Principia), the modern resolution (typed set theory, ZFC foundation axiom). Each is addressed in sibling artifacts — this one makes the paradox walkable.

grammar_alignment.note: russell_set_box teaches self_reference (a form that describes itself) and paradox (a form whose premises contradict). The other two foundations operations are parallel — non-Euclidean breaks the parallel postulate, impossible assembles locally-consistent pieces into a globally-contradictory whole. Together they map the ways mathematics discovers its limits.

biome_alignment.note: The biome is now 95% dense — the world is fully alive, and now it shows its SEAMS. Escher-like geometries, Penrose triangles, places where walking forward brings you back. The 'break' catalyst lets the player introduce a contradiction into any form — and the form persists despite the contradiction. This is the sequence where the world reveals it was never fully consistent.

stages.title: From optimization to self-reference
stages.thinking: ML_Gradient_Landscape taught that learning is descending a landscape of loss. Optimization was meaningful when we knew what 'better' meant — the loss function was given. But what if the SYSTEM ITSELF can’t decide what’s true? What if a well-formed statement in a well-formed system lands on 'both true and false' simultaneously? This is the foundations crisis. Not failure of implementation — failure of the system to be internally consistent.
stages.code:
# Learning: follow the gradient, descend toward minimum
#   requires a LOSS FUNCTION that is well-defined
#   requires a SPACE where 'lower' is meaningful
#
# But what if the space has a HOLE?
# What if a position in parameter space is neither
# up nor down, but BOTH, because the rules contradict?
#
# Russell, 1901: consider S = { x | x ∉ x }
# Is S ∈ S?
#   If yes, then by definition of S, S ∉ S. Contradiction.
#   If no, then by definition of S, S ∈ S. Contradiction.
#
# Neither answer works. The set breaks the system.

stages.title: A box is a set
stages.thinking: Concretize the abstract. A set contains members. A box contains objects. What if a box could contain BOXES? Nothing strange about that. Now: what if a box contains ITSELF? Impossible in physical space — but possible in set theory. Russell’s set is defined precisely as the set of sets that do NOT contain themselves. The question: does this set contain itself? Both answers lead to contradiction. The box artifact makes this feel, physically, like an infinite regress.

stages.title: Opening the box reveals another box
stages.thinking: The first interaction: click the box. It opens. Inside is another, smaller box. Click again: opens. Another box inside. Each box is a copy of the outer — same proportions, smaller scale. After a few levels, the player understands: this is infinite. The regress has no bottom.
stages.code:
var _current_depth: int = 0
var _inner_box: RussellSetBox = null

func _on_box_clicked() -> void:
	if _current_depth >= max_visible_depth:
		_show_infinite_regress()
		infinite_regress_detected.emit()
		return
	
	# Open the lid
	_animate_open()
	
	# Instantiate the next box inside
	if _inner_box == null:
		_inner_box = _spawn_inner_box(_current_depth + 1)
	
	box_opened.emit(_current_depth)

func _spawn_inner_box(depth: int) -> RussellSetBox:
	var inner = RussellSetBox.new()
	inner.size = size * 0.65
	inner.max_visible_depth = max_visible_depth
	inner._current_depth = depth
	inner.position = Vector3.ZERO
	add_child(inner)
	return inner

stages.title: The ∞ indicator — admit the regress
stages.thinking: max_visible_depth = 7. After opening seven boxes, we can’t keep going (performance, clarity). Instead, the 8th box displays the infinity symbol and a text: 'the regress continues.' This is honest. We cannot render infinity, but we can POINT to it. The symbol is not the thing; it is the signal that the thing is endless. The player understands: this is not a bug. This is the paradox being exactly itself.
stages.code:
func _show_infinite_regress() -> void:
	var infinity_label = Label3D.new()
	infinity_label.text = "∞"
	infinity_label.font_size = 96
	infinity_label.pixel_size = 0.002
	infinity_label.modulate = Color(1.0, 0.3, 0.3)  # alert red
	infinity_label.billboard = BaseMaterial3D.BILLBOARD_ENABLED
	infinity_label.position = Vector3(0, 0, 0)
	add_child(infinity_label)
	
	var context_label = Label3D.new()
	context_label.text = "the regress continues\nthe box contains itself\nS ∈ S ↔ S ∉ S"
	context_label.font_size = 16
	context_label.position = Vector3(0, -0.2, 0)
	context_label.modulate = Color(0.9, 0.7, 0.7)
	add_child(context_label)

stages.title: Paradox text escalates with depth
stages.thinking: Each level, a different text appears. Level 1: 'a box.' Level 2: 'a box inside a box.' Level 3: 'and another.' Level 4: 'how deep does this go?' Level 5: 'this is the paradox.' Level 6: 'R = { x | x ∉ x }.' Level 7: 'Is R in R? If yes — contradiction. If no — contradiction.' The text accompanies the embodied experience. The box gives you a body. The text gives you a mind. Together: the paradox lands.
stages.code:
const PARADOX_TEXTS := [
	"a box",
	"a box inside a box",
	"and another",
	"how deep does this go?",
	"this is the paradox",
	"R = { x | x ∉ x }",
	"Is R in R? If yes — contradiction. If no — contradiction.",
]

func _update_paradox_text(depth: int) -> void:
	var idx = mini(depth, PARADOX_TEXTS.size() - 1)
	_label.text = PARADOX_TEXTS[idx]
	# Later texts fade in more slowly, feel more ominous
	_label.modulate = Color(
		0.9,
		0.9 - depth * 0.08,
		0.9 - depth * 0.08,
		1.0
	)

stages.title: The lid opens with a physical animation
stages.thinking: The box opens via a rotating lid (AnimationPlayer or Tween). This matters. If boxes just popped open, the experience would feel arcade. The hinge-rotation animation slows the player down — each opening is a small ritual. You DECIDE to open each layer. You watch the lid turn. You see the inside reveal. The artifact uses time as a teaching tool.
stages.code:
func _animate_open() -> void:
	var tween = create_tween()
	tween.tween_property(
		_lid, "rotation_degrees:x",
		-120.0,  # open angle
		0.6      # duration in seconds
	).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_CUBIC)

# The open duration is calibrated:
#   too fast (< 0.2s)  → feels arcade, no gravity
#   0.6s               → natural hinge feel
#   too slow (> 1.5s)  → boring, player checks out
# Time as pedagogy.

stages.title: Signals let other systems observe the paradox
stages.thinking: box_opened(depth), paradox_observed(depth), infinite_regress_detected() — three signals. Other artifacts in the map (science screens, catalyst devices) can listen and react. The science screen updates with the paradox explanation at each depth. A catalyst target can unlock at infinite_regress_detected. Signals make the artifact composable with the map’s narrative.
stages.code:
signal paradox_observed(depth: int)
signal box_opened(depth: int)
signal infinite_regress_detected()

# In the map:
func _ready() -> void:
	$RussellSetBox.box_opened.connect(_on_box_opened)
	$RussellSetBox.infinite_regress_detected.connect(_on_regress)

func _on_box_opened(depth: int) -> void:
	$ScienceScreen.set_paragraph(depth)

func _on_regress() -> void:
	$CatalystTarget.unlock()
	$DarkSphere.darken_further()

# The paradox is an EVENT other systems can subscribe to.
# The map composes around it.

stages.title: Give it identity
stages.thinking: The Russell set box knows what it is. Not a toy — a physical demonstration that self-reference in naive set theory leads to a contradiction that destroyed the foundations of mathematics in 1901. Russell’s letter to Frege arrived while Frege’s second volume of Grundgesetze was at the printer. Frege inserted an acknowledgment in an afterword that his system was inconsistent. The modern resolution (ZFC, type theory) is elsewhere in the sequence; this artifact offers the crisis itself, unvarnished. The truth: some systems break when they try to describe everything.

# critical_parameter: max_visible_depth — how many nested boxes before the infinite regress indicator
# triggers: click/interact opens next layer; each opening reveals a smaller box; at max depth the ∞ symbol appears; paradox text escalates
